### BASIC keywords

| Keyword | Kind | Syntax | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `END` | statement | `END` | Ends the program, stops background music and returns to the READY prompt. |
| `FOR` | statement | `FOR variable=start TO end [STEP step]` | Starts a loop: sets the variable to start and repeats the body up to NEXT, adding step (default 1) until it passes end; the body runs at least once. |
| `NEXT` | statement | `NEXT [variable[,variable...]]` | Ends a FOR loop: adds the step and loops back while the limit is not passed; NEXT I,J closes several loops in turn. |
| `DATA` | statement | `DATA value[,value...]` | Holds constants that READ takes in program order; executing a DATA statement does nothing. |
| `INPUT` | statement | `INPUT [prompt;] variable[,variable...]` | Reads values typed in the screen editor into variables; program mode only, and an empty line stops the run (CONT resumes). |
| `DIM` | statement | `DIM array(dimensions)[,array...]` | Creates arrays with the given highest subscripts, starting at 0; an array used without DIM gets 0-10 per dimension, and a second DIM gives REDIM'D ARRAY. |
| `READ` | statement | `READ variable[,variable...]` | Assigns the next DATA items, in program order, to the listed variables. |
| `LET` | statement | `[LET] variable=expression` | Assigns an expression to a variable; the word LET is optional. Assigning TI sets the 60 Hz clock. |
| `GOTO` | statement | `GOTO line` | Jumps to the given line number. |
| `RUN` | statement | `RUN [line]` | Clears variables, arrays, strings, the DATA pointer and the FOR/GOSUB stack, then runs the program from its start or from the given line. |
| `IF` | statement | `IF condition THEN line\|statement \| IF condition GOTO line` | Tests a condition: when true it jumps to a line or runs the rest of the line, otherwise it continues with the next line. |
| `RESTORE` | statement | `RESTORE` | Resets the DATA pointer so the next READ starts at the first DATA item; it takes no line number (RESTORE 10 is a SYNTAX ERROR). |
| `GOSUB` | statement | `GOSUB line` | Calls the subroutine at the given line; RETURN resumes after the GOSUB. Nesting too deep gives OUT OF MEMORY. |
| `RETURN` | statement | `RETURN` | Returns from the most recent GOSUB, dropping any FOR loops opened inside it; with no GOSUB active it gives RETURN WITHOUT GOSUB. |
| `REM` | statement | `REM [text]` | Marks the rest of the line as a comment; nothing after REM on that line runs. |
| `STOP` | statement | `STOP` | Stops the program with BREAK IN line and stops background music; CONT resumes after it. Ctrl-C between statements does the same. |
| `ON` | statement | `ON index GOTO\|GOSUB line[,line...]` | Jumps to (GOTO) or calls (GOSUB) the line at position index in the list; 0 or a position past the end continues. |
| `WAIT` | statement | `WAIT address,mask[,invert]` | Pauses until (PEEK(address) XOR invert) AND mask is nonzero; the loop does not check Ctrl-C, so a condition that never comes true hangs the machine. |
| `LOAD` | statement | `LOAD path` | Replaces the program with a tokenized BASIC file from the SD card, clears variables and ends at READY, even when a program runs it. |
| `SAVE` | statement | `SAVE path` | Writes the current program's tokenized text (TXTTAB to VARTAB, no header) to a file on the SD card, creating or truncating it. |
| `DEF` | statement | `DEF FNname(variable)=expression` | Defines a one-argument numeric function FNname for later use in expressions; program mode only (ILLEGAL DIRECT in direct mode). |
| `POKE` | statement | `POKE address,value` | Writes a byte to a CPU memory address. |
| `COLOR` | statement | `COLOR bank` | Sets the BASIC pen palette (0-15) used for READY, error messages, INPUT prompts, numbers and unstyled text; the editor pen is not changed. |
| `FLIPX` | statement | `FLIPX enabled` | Turns the horizontal flip on (nonzero) or off (0) in the BASIC pen used for messages and unstyled output. |
| `FLIPY` | statement | `FLIPY enabled` | Turns the vertical flip on (nonzero) or off (0) in the BASIC pen used for messages and unstyled output. |
| `ALT` | statement | `ALT enabled` | Turns the alternate (reverse) character bank on (nonzero) or off (0) in the BASIC pen used for messages and unstyled output. |
| `STYLE` | statement | `STYLE mask` | Chooses which attribute fields (1 color, 2 flip-X, 4 flip-Y, 8 ALT) printed styled strings take from the BASIC pen instead of their own. |
| `CRSR` | statement | `CRSR column,row` | Moves the text cursor to column 0-39, row 0-24 (0,0 is the top-left corner) and sets BASIC's column counter to match. |
| `CLS` | statement | `CLS` | Clears the screen, homes the cursor and resets BASIC's column counter to 0. |
| `PRINT` | statement | `PRINT [expression][,\|;expression...]` | Prints values; strings keep their stored per-character colors and attributes, while numbers and unstyled text use the BASIC pen set by COLOR. |
| `CONT` | statement | `CONT` | Continues a program stopped by STOP, Ctrl-C or an empty INPUT line; after an error, a program edit, NEW, CLEAR, RUN or LOAD it gives CAN'T CONTINUE. |
| `LIST` | statement | `LIST [start][-[end]]` | Lists program lines, all or a range, with string literals in their stored colors, then returns to READY (a LIST inside a program ends the run). |
| `CLEAR` | statement | `CLEAR` | Clears all variables, arrays and strings and resets the DATA pointer and FOR/GOSUB stack; Clementina spells it CLEAR (not CLR) and it takes no argument. |
| `GET` | statement | `GET variable[,variable...]` | Waits for a key for each variable and stores it without echo; program mode only (ILLEGAL DIRECT in direct mode). |
| `NEW` | statement | `NEW` | Erases the program and all variables and stops background music; inside a running program it also ends the run. |
| `TAB(` | function | `TAB(column)` | Inside PRINT, prints spaces up to the given column; it is not valid elsewhere and returns no value. |
| `TO` | keyword | `FOR variable=start TO end \| GO TO line` | Separates the start value from the limit in FOR, and follows GO in GO TO; it is not a statement by itself. |
| `FN` | function | `FNname(argument)` | Calls a function defined with DEF FNname, passing one numeric argument; an undefined name gives UNDEF'D FUNCTION. |
| `SPC(` | function | `SPC(count)` | Inside PRINT, prints the given number of spaces (0-255); it is not valid elsewhere and returns no value. |
| `THEN` | keyword | `IF condition THEN line\|statement` | Follows the condition in IF; GOTO may stand in its place when jumping to a line. |
| `NOT` | operator | `NOT value` | Bitwise NOT of a 16-bit integer, giving -value-1, so NOT 0 is -1 (true) and NOT -1 is 0 (false). |
| `STEP` | keyword | `FOR variable=start TO end STEP step` | Sets the amount added to the FOR variable on each NEXT (default 1); a negative step counts down. |
| `+` | operator | `left + right \| +right` | Adds two numbers or joins two strings (up to 255 characters); a leading + is ignored. |
| `-` | operator | `left - right \| -right` | Subtracts two numbers or negates one; negation binds tighter than * and / but looser than ^, so -2^2 is -4. |
| `*` | operator | `left * right` | Multiplies two numbers; a result too large for the float format gives OVERFLOW. |
| `/` | operator | `left / right` | Divides the left number by the right; dividing by zero gives DIVISION BY ZERO. |
| `^` | operator | `left ^ right` | Raises a number to a power, with the highest precedence; a negative base needs an integer exponent, otherwise ILLEGAL QUANTITY. |
| `AND` | operator | `left AND right` | Bitwise AND of two 16-bit integers; applied to comparison results (-1 or 0) it acts as logical AND. |
| `OR` | operator | `left OR right` | Bitwise OR of two 16-bit integers; applied to comparison results (-1 or 0) it acts as logical OR; it binds looser than AND. |
| `>` | operator | `left > right` | Greater-than comparison of two numbers or two strings (by character code), giving -1 if true and 0 if false. |
| `=` | operator | `left = right` | Equality comparison of two numbers or two strings (by character code), giving -1 if true and 0 if false. |
| `<` | operator | `left < right` | Less-than comparison of two numbers or two strings (by character code), giving -1 if true and 0 if false. |
| `SGN` | function | `SGN(number)` | Returns -1, 0 or 1 for a negative, zero or positive number. |
| `INT` | function | `INT(number)` | Returns the largest integer not greater than the number (floor), so INT(-1.5) is -2. |
| `ABS` | function | `ABS(number)` | Returns the absolute value of a number. |
| `USR` | function | `USR(value)` | Calls the machine-code routine named by the USR vector in zero page, passing the argument in the floating-point accumulator. |
| `FRE` | function | `FRE(value)` | Collects unused strings and returns the free bytes between the arrays and the string heap; the argument is ignored. |
| `POS` | function | `POS(value)` | Returns BASIC's output column counter (0-255); the argument is ignored. |
| `SQR` | function | `SQR(number)` | Returns the square root, computed as X^0.5; a negative argument gives ILLEGAL QUANTITY. |
| `RND` | function | `RND(number)` | Returns a pseudo-random number from 0 up to 1: a positive argument gives the next one, 0 repeats the last, a negative one reseeds. |
| `LOG` | function | `LOG(number)` | Returns the natural logarithm; the argument must be greater than 0, else ILLEGAL QUANTITY. |
| `EXP` | function | `EXP(number)` | Returns e raised to the number; results beyond the float range (argument above about 88.03) give OVERFLOW. |
| `COS` | function | `COS(number)` | Returns the cosine of an angle in radians. |
| `SIN` | function | `SIN(number)` | Returns the sine of an angle in radians. |
| `TAN` | function | `TAN(number)` | Returns the tangent of an angle in radians. |
| `ATN` | function | `ATN(number)` | Returns the arctangent, in radians, between -PI/2 and PI/2. |
| `PEEK` | function | `PEEK(address)` | Returns the byte (0-255) at a CPU memory address. |
| `LEN` | function | `LEN(string)` | Returns the number of characters in a string (0-255). |
| `STR$` | function | `STR$(number)` | Converts a number to the text PRINT would show, with a leading space for positive numbers or a minus sign. |
| `VAL` | function | `VAL(string)` | Converts the leading decimal number in a string to its value, or 0 if there is none; hex $ prefixes are not recognized. |
| `ASC` | function | `ASC(string)` | Returns the code (0-255) of the first character of a string; an empty string gives ILLEGAL QUANTITY. |
| `CHR$` | function | `CHR$(code)` | Returns a one-character string with the given code (0-255). |
| `LEFT$` | function | `LEFT$(string, length)` | Returns the leftmost length characters of a string (all of it if shorter), keeping their attributes. |
| `RIGHT$` | function | `RIGHT$(string, length)` | Returns the rightmost length characters of a string (all of it if shorter), keeping their attributes. |
| `MID$` | function | `MID$(string, start[, length])` | Returns length characters of a string starting at position start (1-based), or the rest of the string when length is omitted. |
| `GO` | statement | `GO TO line` | Two-word form of GOTO, written GO TO line; GO SUB is not supported. |
| `MON` | statement | `MON` | Enters the WozMon machine-code monitor; typing Q there returns to BASIC's READY prompt with the program and variables kept. |
| `BCOLOR` | statement | `BCOLOR bank` | Sets the screen backdrop to the ink color of a palette bank, the same color COLOR gives text. |
| `SNDON` | statement | `SNDON` | Starts the MIA sound generator (audio starts stopped); set voices up first, then SNDON once. |
| `SNDOFF` | statement | `SNDOFF` | Stops the sound generator; voice registers are kept. |
| `SNDCLR` | statement | `SNDCLR` | Stops the sound generator, clears every voice and restores the audio defaults. |
| `VOL` | statement | `VOL level \| voice,level` | Sets the master volume (0-15), or with a voice number sets that voice's volume trim (0-255, 255 = unity). |
| `WAVE` | statement | `WAVE voice,waveform` | Selects a voice's waveform: 0 sine, 1 pulse, 2 saw, 3 triangle or 4 noise. |
| `NOTE` | statement | `NOTE voice,note` | Plays a semitone (0-95) on a voice, starting a new note with its envelope and waveform restarted. |
| `FREQ` | statement | `FREQ voice,hz` | Sets a voice's pitch in whole hertz (0-4095) without restarting the note. |
| `GATE` | statement | `GATE voice,enabled` | Gates a voice's note on without retriggering (non-zero) or releases it so it fades out (0). |
| `ADSR` | statement | `ADSR voice,attack,decay,sustain,release` | Sets a voice's envelope: attack, decay and release rates and the sustain level, each 0-15. |
| `PULSE` | statement | `PULSE voice,width` | Sets a voice's pulse duty cycle (0-255, 128 about square); only affects the pulse waveform. |
| `PAN` | statement | `PAN voice,position` | Sets a voice's stereo position from -64 (hard left) through 0 (centre) to 63 (hard right). |
| `BGON` | statement | `BGON` | Turns the background (playfield) layer on. |
| `BGOFF` | statement | `BGOFF` | Turns the background (playfield) layer off. |
| `BGMODE` | statement | `BGMODE mode` | Selects how the background's raw 40x25 tables tile into one scrollable map (modes 0-5). |
| `BGSET` | statement | `BGSET set` | Selects which of the two background table sets (0 or 1) the current BGMODE arrangement is drawn from. |
| `SCROLL` | statement | `SCROLL x,y` | Pans the 320x200 view across the background map by x,y pixels, wrapping at the map's edges. |
| `BGBANK` | statement | `BGBANK bank` | Selects the CHR bank (0-7) the background layer normally draws its tiles from. |
| `BGALT` | statement | `BGALT bank` | Selects the CHR bank (0-7) used for background cells whose attribute has the CHR_ALT bit set. |
| `SPRON` | statement | `SPRON` | Turns the whole sprite layer on. |
| `SPROFF` | statement | `SPROFF` | Turns the whole sprite layer off. |
| `SPRCOUNT` | statement | `SPRCOUNT lastIndex` | Sets the highest sprite (OAM) index, 0-255, that the renderer scans each frame. |
| `SPRBANK` | statement | `SPRBANK bank` | Selects the CHR bank (0-7) that sprites draw their tiles from. |
| `CHRMODE` | statement | `CHRMODE bank,is1bpp` | Marks a CHR bank (0-7) as 1bpp two-color graphics (non-zero) or 3bpp eight-color graphics (0). |
| `CHRPLANE` | statement | `CHRPLANE background,sprites,overlay` | Chooses which plane of a 1bpp CHR bank the background, sprite and overlay layers each decode (0-2). |
| `PALETTE` | statement | `PALETTE bank,index,red,green,blue` | Writes one palette color: bank 0-15, color index 0-7, as RGB565 with red 0-31, green 0-63 and blue 0-31. |
| `VIDON` | statement | `VIDON` | Turns the whole video output on. |
| `VIDOFF` | statement | `VIDOFF` | Turns the whole video output off. |
| `BGCHAR` | statement | `BGCHAR column,row,tile,attribute` | Writes one background cell (tile and attribute) at a map position for the current BGMODE, finding the right raw table. |
| `CHRLOAD` | statement | `CHRLOAD path,bank[,offset]` | Loads a whole SD card file into a CHR bank, starting offset bytes into it. |
| `PALLOAD` | statement | `PALLOAD path,bank[,offset]` | Loads a whole SD card file of RGB565 bytes into palette RAM, starting offset bytes into a palette bank. |
| `OAMLOAD` | statement | `OAMLOAD path[,index]` | Loads a whole SD card file of 5-byte sprite records into OAM, starting at sprite index. |
| `SPRITE` | statement | `SPRITE index,tile,x,y,palette,flags` | Sets up one sprite completely: tile, signed x and y position, palette and flag bits (hide, priority, flips). |
| `SPRTILE` | statement | `SPRTILE index,tile` | Changes only one sprite's tile (animation frame), leaving its other settings alone. |
| `SPRX` | statement | `SPRX index,x` | Changes only one sprite's X position (-512 to 511), leaving its other settings alone. |
| `SPRY` | statement | `SPRY index,y` | Changes only one sprite's Y position (-256 to 255), leaving its other settings alone. |
| `SPRCOLOR` | statement | `SPRCOLOR index,palette` | Changes only one sprite's palette (0-15), leaving its priority and flip bits alone. |
| `SPRFLIP` | statement | `SPRFLIP index,flipX,flipY` | Changes only one sprite's horizontal and vertical flip (each 0 or non-zero), leaving its other bits alone. |
| `SPRPRI` | statement | `SPRPRI index,priority` | Changes only one sprite's priority bit (0 or non-zero), leaving its palette and flips alone. |
| `OPEN` | statement | `OPEN path FOR mode AS #handle` | Opens an SD card file as file number 1-16 for INPUT, OUTPUT, APPEND or UPDATE. |
| `CLOSE` | statement | `CLOSE #handle` | Closes file number 1-16, flushing anything written to it. |
| `BGET#` | statement | `BGET# handle,variable` | Reads one byte (0-255) from an open file into a numeric variable. |
| `BPUT#` | statement | `BPUT# handle,value` | Writes one byte (0-255) to an open file. |
| `BANK` | statement | `BANK bank` | Picks the bank that BLOAD, BRUN, BSAVE, PEEK, POKE and SYS use at $8000-$BFFF; each maps it only while it works there, then maps bank 0 back. |
| `BRUN` | statement | `BRUN path[,run]` | Loads a PRG file at its header address and jumps to it, with the BANK bank mapped; it never returns to BASIC. |
| `NTREAD` | statement | `NTREAD table,cell,count` | Copies count tile bytes from the current DATA position into a background nametable, starting at cell. |
| `NTLOAD` | statement | `NTLOAD path,table[,cell]` | Loads a whole file into a background table's nametable, starting at cell. |
| `NTSAVE` | statement | `NTSAVE path,table[,cell[,count]]` | Saves count bytes of a background table's nametable, or the rest of the table, starting at cell, to a file. |
| `ATRREAD` | statement | `ATRREAD table,cell,count` | Copies count attribute bytes from the current DATA position into a background table's attribute plane, starting at cell. |
| `ATRLOAD` | statement | `ATRLOAD path,table[,cell]` | Loads a whole file into a background table's attribute plane, starting at cell. |
| `ATRSAVE` | statement | `ATRSAVE path,table[,cell[,count]]` | Saves count bytes of a background table's attribute plane, or the rest of the table, starting at cell, to a file. |
| `CHRREAD` | statement | `CHRREAD bank,offset,count` | Copies count graphics bytes from the current DATA position into a CHR bank, starting at byte offset. |
| `CHRSAVE` | statement | `CHRSAVE path,bank[,offset[,count]]` | Saves count bytes of a CHR bank, or the rest of the bank, starting at byte offset, to a file. |
| `PALREAD` | statement | `PALREAD bank,offset,count` | Copies count raw RGB565 palette bytes from the current DATA position into a palette bank, starting at offset. |
| `PALSAVE` | statement | `PALSAVE path,bank[,offset[,count]]` | Saves count raw palette bytes, or the rest of the palette bank, starting at offset, to a file. |
| `OAMREAD` | statement | `OAMREAD index,count` | Copies count 5-byte sprite records from the current DATA position into OAM starting at sprite index. |
| `OAMSAVE` | statement | `OAMSAVE path[,index[,count]]` | Saves count 5-byte sprite records, or the rest of the 256, starting at OAM index, to a file. |
| `MIALOAD` | statement | `MIALOAD path,address` | Loads a whole file straight into MIA RAM at a raw address, stopping at the end of the file or of MIA RAM. |
| `MIASAVE` | statement | `MIASAVE path,address,length` | Saves length bytes of MIA RAM starting at a raw address to a file. |
| `SEEK#` | statement | `SEEK# handle,position` | Sets the read and write position of an open file to a byte offset. |
| `KILL` | statement | `KILL path` | Deletes a file, or an empty directory, on the SD card. |
| `RMDIR` | statement | `RMDIR path` | Removes an empty directory on the SD card; it shares KILL's routine, so it also deletes a file. |
| `MKDIR` | statement | `MKDIR path` | Creates one directory; its parent must already exist. |
| `NAME` | statement | `NAME oldPath AS newPath` | Renames or moves a file or directory. |
| `CD` | statement | `CD path` | Changes the current directory used to resolve relative paths. |
| `DIR` | statement | `DIR [path]` | Lists the current directory, or the given directory, one name per line with a trailing slash on directories. |
| `INPUTMODE` | statement | `INPUTMODE mode` | Selects the input source (console, Wi-Fi or USB keyboard), if MIA reports it available. |
| `KEYCLEAR` | statement | `KEYCLEAR` | Discards the text bytes currently queued in the input FIFO, leaving held-key state alone. |
| `KEYREPEAT` | statement | `KEYREPEAT delay,interval \| 0` | Sets MIA key-repeat delay and interval in milliseconds, or disables repeat with 0. |
| `KEYRPT` | statement | `KEYRPT code,enabled` | Enables or disables key repeat for one keyboard HID usage code. |
| `MOUSE` | statement | `MOUSE deltaX,deltaY,buttons,wheel,pan` | Reads relative mouse motion, buttons, wheel and pan into five numeric variables. |
| `PADREAD` | statement | `PADREAD pad` | Samples a gamepad slot into BASIC's cache for the PAD functions. |
| `OVLON` | statement | `OVLON` | Shows the overlay (text console) layer. |
| `OVLOFF` | statement | `OVLOFF` | Hides the overlay (text console) layer without clearing it. |
| `OVLBANK` | statement | `OVLBANK bank` | Selects the primary CHR bank the overlay layer draws from. |
| `OVLALT` | statement | `OVLALT bank` | Selects the alternate CHR bank used by overlay cells with the ALT attribute bit. |
| `DELAY` | statement | `DELAY milliseconds` | Waits the given number of milliseconds using MIA's wall clock; Ctrl-C can interrupt. |
| `MPOKE` | statement | `MPOKE address,value` | Writes one byte to a MIA RAM address. |
| `MCOPY` | statement | `MCOPY source,destination,length[,rows,sourceStride,destinationStride]` | Copies a block, or a rectangle of rows, within MIA RAM. |
| `MFILL` | statement | `MFILL address,length,value[,rows,stride]` | Fills a block, or a rectangle of rows, of MIA RAM with one byte value. |
| `FLUSH` | statement | `FLUSH #handle` | Flushes an open file's pending data and metadata to the SD card without closing it. |
| `FSTAT` | statement | `FSTAT path,size,attributes,date,time` | Reads a file's size, FAT attributes, packed date and packed time into four numeric variables. |
| `BLOAD` | statement | `BLOAD path[,address]` | Loads a PRG file into CPU RAM at its header address or another address, then returns to BASIC. |
| `BSAVE` | statement | `BSAVE path,address,length` | Saves length bytes of CPU RAM from address to a file in BLOAD's format, a 2-byte address header and the data. |
| `SYS` | statement | `SYS address` | Calls a machine-code subroutine at a CPU address with JSR and continues after it returns. |
| `TRACK` | statement | `TRACK voice,music[,address]` | Compiles a music string into a voice's background sequencer track in MIA RAM. |
| `BAND` | statement | `BAND enabled \| voice,enabled` | Starts or stops background sequencer playback for all voices or for one voice. |
| `VTAKE` | statement | `VTAKE voice` | Freezes a voice's background track without silencing it so the program can drive the voice directly. |
| `VGIVE` | statement | `VGIVE voice` | Returns a voice taken with VTAKE to its background track, catching up to the shared clock. |
| `PLAYING` | function | `PLAYING(voice)` | Returns 1 while a voice's background sequencer track is running, else 0. |
| `EOF` | function | `EOF(handle)` | Returns 1 when an open file is at its end, else 0. |
| `KEYDOWN` | function | `KEYDOWN(code)` | Returns 1 if the keyboard HID usage code is currently held, else 0. |
| `CONSDOWN` | function | `CONSDOWN(code)` | Returns 1 if the consumer-page HID usage code is currently held, else 0. |
| `INPUTDEV` | function | `INPUTDEV(dummy)` | Returns MIA's live input capability bit mask (keyboard, consumer, mouse, gamepads). |
| `PADON` | function | `PADON(pad)` | Returns 1 if the last PADREAD sample shows the gamepad connected, else 0. |
| `PADDIR` | function | `PADDIR(pad)` | Returns the D-pad direction bits from the last PADREAD sample of a gamepad. |
| `PADSTICK` | function | `PADSTICK(pad)` | Returns the digital stick direction bits from the last PADREAD sample of a gamepad. |
| `PADBTN` | function | `PADBTN(pad, button)` | Returns 1 if a button is pressed in the last PADREAD sample of a gamepad, else 0. |
| `PADAXIS` | function | `PADAXIS(pad, axis)` | Returns an analog axis value, -128 to 127, from the last PADREAD sample of a gamepad. |
| `PADTRIG` | function | `PADTRIG(pad, trigger)` | Returns an analog trigger value, 0 to 255, from the last PADREAD sample of a gamepad. |
| `TICKS` | function | `TICKS(dummy)` | Returns milliseconds since MIA's last runtime reset, modulo 2^32. |
| `MPEEK` | function | `MPEEK(address)` | Returns the byte at a MIA RAM address. |
| `FPOS` | function | `FPOS(handle)` | Returns the current byte position in an open file. |
| `FSIZE` | function | `FSIZE(handle)` | Returns the size in bytes of an open file. |
| `DISKFREE` | function | `DISKFREE(volume)` | Returns the free bytes on the current SD volume. |
| `CUE` | function | `CUE(voice)` | Returns how many notes, ties and rests a voice's background track has played since it was loaded (0 before it starts). |
